summary: Iteration 13 backend-only testing: Pro entitlements + dish rename propagation. 20/21 new tests pass (test_iteration13_pro_and_rename.py) and 48/48 iteration-11+12 regression tests pass (one transient ConnectTimeout on public URL that passed on retry — same known flake noted in iteration 12). Verified: (a) /auth/me, register, login all expose new fields `is_pro` and `pro_source`; (b) FOUNDER_USERNAMES whitelist (halley/matteo/admin) marks users is_pro:true, pro_source:'founder' with case-insensitive registration (Halley/HALLEY/halley all normalize); (c) admin POST /api/admin/users/{id}/entitlements/pro with {active:true, reason} grants pro (pro_source:'admin_grant', granted_at set) and PUT /auth/preferences afterward does NOT wipe entitlements; (d) POST with {active:false} correctly sets is_pro:false; (e) missing X-Admin-Password → 401, wrong password → 401, unknown user_id → 404; (f) founder whitelist wins over admin revoke (still is_pro:true after admin sets active:false); (g) PUT /dishes/{id} with a new name propagates dish_name across weekly_plans.slots.items[] (including across multiple weeks and multi-item slots) and shopping_items.sources[] (both ingredient rows updated); (h) renaming an orphan dish (not in any slot/shopping) succeeds; (i) PUT with unchanged name is idempotent; (j) non-name changes (course/preparation/notes/servings/ingredients) leave planner items[] dish_name and shopping_items.sources[] untouched, and planner_qty is unchanged (slot is not re-applied); (k) cross-user isolation preserved — user A's rename does not touch user B's planner even when both users have a dish also called Alpha. Found ONE minor inconsistency in `_user_public` (server.py:351): after admin revoke, `is_pro` is False (correct) but `pro_source` still returns 'admin_grant' because the fallback `pro_ent.get('source')` is truthy regardless of active. Fresh non-founder users correctly return pro_source:null. Recommend the code read pro_source only when is_pro is true.

minor.issue: After POST /api/admin/users/{id}/entitlements/pro with active:false, response has is_pro:false (correct) but pro_source:'admin_grant' instead of null. server.py:351 uses `pro_ent.get('source') or (...)` which returns the stored source even when active is False. Fix suggestion: gate pro_source on is_pro (e.g., `'admin_grant' if pro_ent.get('active') else None`). Fresh non-founder users are unaffected because they have no entitlements dict.

action_items: Fix pro_source computation in server.py:_user_public so it is null when is_pro is False (see minor issue). Concretely: `'founder' if is_founder else ('admin_grant' if pro_ent.get('active') else None)` — or gate on `is_pro` as a whole.
(Carried over from iter-12, still valid) admin.require_admin should use secrets.compare_digest for constant-time comparison of X-Admin-Password.

(Optional) Consider updating slot items[].course in planner when the dish's course changes (currently only name is propagated; course is cached from slot-put time). Not part of iteration-13 spec but likely surprising to users.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:670-696 (update_dish rename propagation): iterates all user weekly_plans and rewrites full `slots` dict per plan when any item matches. Fine at current scale but O(P*S*I) per rename. If a user ever accumulates dozens of weeks with dense slots, consider a targeted query like `slots.<key>.items.dish_id == id` combined with an $[] array-filter update analogous to the shopping_items update on line 692. That would be one atomic update rather than N read-modify-writes.

server.py:692-696 uses `sources.$[s].dish_name` with array_filters — this is the right pattern; consider applying the same idea to weekly_plans (dot-path per slot key is harder because slot keys are dynamic, so current per-plan loop is acceptable).
server.py:351 pro_source fallback logic — see the minor issue.
admin.py:131-146 entitlement writes: {reason: ''} is stored even when caller omits reason. Consider only storing reason when non-empty to keep DB tidy.

admin.py:139/141 sets `granted_at` vs `revoked_at` but the previous state's timestamp is silently overwritten (a granted-then-revoked entry loses the granted_at). If audit trail matters, keep both timestamps and add a history array.
server.py is now 1316 lines — approaches the 2000-line soft cap; recommend splitting routers (auth, dishes, planner, shopping, admin-adjacent) into separate modules soon.

success_rate.backend: 95% (20/21 new tests; the 1 failure is a real minor bug in pro_source after revoke). Regression: 48/48.

TestFounderWhitelist and TestAdminEntitlementEndpoint.test_founder_admin_grant_is_still_pro_after_revoke first DELETE any existing halley/matteo/admin user via /api/admin/users to make the tests idempotent, and clean up afterward. rca_of_issue: Bug in server.py:351 `pro_source` computation. Current: `pro_source = 'founder' if is_founder else (pro_ent.get('source') or ('admin_grant' if pro_ent.get('active') else None))`. Once admin sets active=false, the stored doc becomes {active: False, source: 'admin_grant', ...}. `pro_ent.get('source')` returns 'admin_grant' (truthy) so the `or` short-circuits and pro_source stays 'admin_grant'. Reproduction: register user; POST /api/admin/users/{id}/entitlements/pro {active:true}; POST same {active:false}; GET /auth/me → is_pro:false but pro_source:'admin_grant'. Fix: `pro_source = 'founder' if is_founder else ('admin_grant' if pro_ent.get('active') else None)` (drop the `or` fallback to stored source, since the only non-founder source is admin_grant today anyway).
